jobs.title: AVP, Data Governance
jobs.description:
Job Title

AVP, Data Governance

Job Description

Role Overview

Pacific Life Re is progressing a major business, technology and data transformation across Divisional Business Services. The Divisional Data Team is delivering the governed data foundations, warehouse, data governance & quality, and reporting capabilities required to support Project Unify, regulatory and management reporting, operational resilience and future analytics including AI enablement.

The AVP, Head of Data Governance role provides strategic and delivery leadership for data governance and data quality across Pacific Life Re. The role translates the Data Strategy and Data Governance and Management Programme into practical standards, controls, operating practices and measurable outcomes, ensuring that data is trusted, understood, appropriately controlled and fit for operational, regulatory and strategic use.

Working with and across all business functions, Technology, Risk, Legal, Compliance, Internal Audit and Pacific Life enterprise teams. The role embeds governance into our business-as-usual practices and project delivery, considering the wider information management lifecycle, including data management, handling, security, privacy, retention and ensures alignment with enterprise divisions. A central expectation is to communicate progress, risks, dependencies, decisions and business outcomes clearly to executive sponsors, governance forums, delivery teams and data users.

This role and is on-site 4 days per week and work from home 1 day per week in Toronto, ON.

Role Responsibilities

Strategy, framework and accountability

Lead the execution of the divisional Data Governance strategy, framework, operating model and roadmap, aligned with the PL Re Data Strategy and relevant enterprise standards.
Develop and maintain clear decision rights, accountability and escalation routes across Data Owners, Business Data Managers, Data Stewards, Business Process Owners and Technology Owners.
Chair the Data Governance Forum and ensure that decisions, actions, standards, exceptions and escalations are recorded, communicated and progressed.
Define and report measures for governance maturity, adoption, control effectiveness and the resolution of material data issues.

Programme delivery

Support the VP for Data, in delivering the Data Governance and Management Programme, including mobilisation, analysis, target-state design, investment planning, prioritised remediation and transition into sustainable implementation.
In collaboration with strategic projects and business workstreams, embed data requirements, definitions, ownership, quality thresholds, lineage, controls, acceptance criteria and governance sign-off throughout delivery.
Maintain an integrated delivery view of milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, resources, budgets, benefits and readiness, escalating decisions promptly and constructively.
Provide executive sponsors and governance bodies with concise, evidence-based updates on progress, outcomes, residual risks and decisions required.

Data Quality

Develop and implement the divisional data quality strategy and operating model, covering critical data, quality rules, measures, controls, scorecards, root-cause analysis and remediation prioritisation.
Lead the adoption of metadata, business glossary, lineage and data catalogue capabilities, ensuring that priority data assets are discoverable, consistently defined and supported by accountable business roles.
In collaboration with Business Analysts, Data Engineering, Reporting and Architecture, embed governance by design into data products, semantic models, workspaces and reporting solutions.
Direct the effective use and integration of strategic governance and data quality technologies, including Collibra and Informatica IDMC, with a focus on control outcomes and business adoption.

Risk, lifecycle & assurance

Lead data lifecycle governance, including retention, classification, discoverability, permitted access, defensible disposition and remediation of identified control gaps.
Act as the senior Data Governance contact for regulatory, audit and risk activity, coordinating evidence, management responses, remediation plans and reporting through the appropriate governance routes.
In collaboration with Legal, Data Protection, Information Security, Risk and Technology, translate policy and regulatory requirements into proportionate, implementable data controls.
Monitor material data risks and issues, challenge remediation plans and support accountable business and technology leaders in reaching documented decisions on residual risk. Working closely with legal and risk functions.

People, engagement and capability

Build and lead a high-performing Data Governance team, setting clear objectives, developing capability, delegating effectively and creating succession depth.
Develop and maintain an engagement and communication plan that translates governance priorities into clear executive narratives, adoption messages, training and role-based guidance.
Establish and support an active stewardship community that shares good practice, resolves cross-functional issues and embeds governance in day-to-day business activity.
Manage specialist partners and contractors against clear deliverables, quality expectations, knowledge-transfer requirements and value outcomes.

Skills & Experience

Extensive experience in data governance, data management, data quality and data leadership within a complex, regulated organisation.
Demonstrable success in moving governance from policy and framework design into practical delivery, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.
Strong programme and change delivery experience, with the ability to coordinate concurrent workstreams, dependencies, risks, resources and budgets.
Strong knowledge of data ownership and stewardship, metadata, business glossaries, lineage, data quality, controls, retention, classification and information lifecycle management.
Practical knowledge of governance and quality technologies, ideally Collibra, Informatica IDMC, Snowflake and Power BI.
Experience supporting regulatory reporting, audit, risk and control remediation in financial services, ideally insurance or reinsurance.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive updates, decision papers, roadmaps, programme communications and adoption materials.
Strong people leadership, coaching and capability-building skills, including experience developing federated communities as well as direct teams.
Relevant professional qualification, such as CDMP or an equivalent data-management credential; recognised programme, risk or change qualifications would be advantageous.

Competencies and Behaviours

Strategic and outcome-focused, with the delivery discipline to convert direction into measurable progress.
Creates clarity from complexity and connects governance, data quality, engineering, reporting, risk and change into a coherent agenda.
Visible and accountable, surfacing risks and dependencies early and following through on commitments.
Commercial and pragmatic, applying proportionate governance that protects the business without creating unnecessary delivery friction.
Collaborative and influential, building shared accountability across business and technology teams.
Communicates with precision and adapts messages for executives, delivery teams and business users.
Develops others, delegates effectively and builds sustainable organisational capability.
Demonstrates integrity, sound judgement and resilience when operating with ambiguity, scrutiny and competing priorities.

Salary Range: $180,000 CAD - $200,000 CAD

Compensation Range

The compensation range noted represents the company’s good faith minimum and maximum range for this role at the time of posting. The actual compensation offered to a candidate will be dependent upon several factors, including but not limited to experience, qualifications and geographic location.

Working For Pacific Life Re

Every person in our global team is valued for the unique qualities they bring to our business and we seek to build their expertise and support their individual ambitions at every step. We work hard and thrive on achievement, but we also know how to have fun and relax too. We regularly host a range of team building days to strengthen our team's connection with each other and reflect on their successes.

Providing employees with a healthy work-life balance is very important to our culture. We have a wide range of employee benefits and we host regular social activities and well being initiatives. We are also committed to supporting our employee's involvement in their communities, by actively fundraising, hosting charity events and overseeing volunteering opportunities.

Benefits

Leave

23 days of annual leave (Regular employees) with option to buy or sell more days
Fertility leave
Generous parental leave

Healthcare

Group Life Insurance and Accidental Death & Dismemberment coverage for all permanent employees
Dental & Optical benefits

Savings & Retirement

RRSP: company-matched contributions

Wellness

Employee and Family Assistance Program
Subsidized gym membership
Time off for volunteering
Charitable matching of employee donations

﻿As part of our commitment to diversity and inclusion, we will provide reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process to ensure equal access to applicants with disabilities. Please contact us about your needs so that we can discuss these with you to make sure that suitable adjustments are made, where possible.

Pacific Life Re Values

Please click here to view our company values

Use of AI

These tools help us identify relevant qualifications and streamline evaluations, but final decisions are always made by our hiring team.

jobs.title: Director, Supply Chain Management
jobs.description:
Position Summary...
The Director, Supply Chain Management is responsible for developing and implementing supply chain strategies, optimizing processes, and managing major projects to ensure efficient operations and superior customer experience across all channels.

What You'll Do...

The Director, Supply Chain Management oversees the design and implementation of end-to-end supply chain planning capabilities, infrastructure, and technology programs, managing annual budgets exceeding $100M. This role develops new tools and processes to optimize flow, inventory, capacity, service, and cost across the supply chain, leveraging global relationships and best practices while using data, analytics, and scenario modelling to inform strategic decisions.

This position leads a team responsible for creating and validating integrated supply chain plans and forecasts, aligning logistics, replenishment, store operations, and eCommerce activities. The Director also manages strategic activities such as seasonal and promotional flow plans, collaborating with 3PL partners and internal teams to balance customer availability, operational capacity, inventory, speed, and cost-effectiveness.

The Director develops supply chain strategy and leads major transformation initiatives, ensuring strong execution, financial governance, and regulatory compliance. The role coordinates cross-functional teams, evaluates end-to-end business trade-offs, oversees progress against strategic objectives, and drives continuous improvement across the supply chain network.

Additionally, the Director develops and maintains critical external partnerships, improves the end-to-end customer experience, and integrates planning and operational processes across the broader supply chain to enhance speed, quality, availability, and cost. This position plays a vital role in the strategic alignment, transformation, and operational excellence of the end-to-end supply chain network.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business, Operations, Finance, Analytics, or a related discipline.
10+ years of progressive experience in supply chain, retail operations, logistics, replenishment, or planning, including significant people leadership experience.
Demonstrated experience leading end-to-end supply chain planning and strategy, connecting demand, inventory, transportation, distribution center capacity, store operations, and eCommerce to deliver business and customer objectives.
Strong expertise in integrated planning, forecasting, inventory and flow management, capacity planning, and network optimization, with the ability to translate long-term growth into actionable supply chain plans.
Proven experience leading large-scale transformation and technology initiatives, including planning platforms, automation, advanced analytics, and/or AI-enabled capabilities, while managing significant budgets and complex programs.
Strong analytical and financial acumen, with experience using scenario modelling, business cases, and financial analysis to optimize trade-offs across service, availability, inventory, capacity, productivity, cost, and ROI.
Demonstrated ability to lead through influence across complex, cross-functional organizations, including Merchandising, Replenishment, Supply Chain, Transportation, Store Operations, eCommerce, Finance, Technology, suppliers, and external partners.
Strong people leadership and executive communication skills, with demonstrated success building high-performing teams, developing talent, leading through change, and influencing senior-level decisions.

Leadership Expectations

Respect the Individual:

Builds high-performing teams; seeks, and embraces differences in people, cultures, ideas and experiences; creates a workplace and experiences where all associates feel seen, supported and connected through culture of belonging so associates thrive and perform; drives a positive associate and customer experience for all.

Creates a discipline and focus around developing talent through feedback, coaching, mentoring, and developmental opportunities; builds the talent pipeline, fosters an environment allowing everyone to bring their best selves to work, empowers associates and partners to act in the best interest of the customer and company, and regularly recognizes others’ contributions and accomplishments; supports strategies and drives initiatives that attract and retain the best talent.

Builds strong and trusting relationships with team members and business partners; works collaboratively and cross-functionally to achieve objectives; and communicates and listens attentively, with energy and positivity to motivate, influence, and inspire commitment and action.

Acts With Integrity

Maintains and promotes the highest standards of integrity, ethics and compliance; models the Walmart values and leads by example to foster our culture; supports Walmart’s goal of becoming a regenerative company by taking action to advance opportunity, sustainability, community, and integrity (e.g., creating fair opportunities for associates and suppliers, driving local giving efforts).

Ensures that teams follow the law, our code of conduct and company policies; promotes an environment where associates feel comfortable sharing concerns, and models our culture of non-retaliation; listens to concerns raised by associates and takes action, and enables others to do the same; holds self and teams accountable for achieving results in a way that is consistent with our values.

Acts as an altruistic servant leader and is consistently humble, self-aware.

Serve Our Customers

Delivers expected business results while putting the customer first and consistently applying an omni-merchant mindset and acting with an Every Day Low Cost mindset to drive value and Every Day Low Prices for customers.

Adopts a holistic perspective that considers data, analytics, customer insights, and different parts of the business when making plans and implementing strategies.

Strive For Excellence

Consistently raises the bar and seeks to improve; demonstrates curiosity and a growth mindset; seeks feedback, asks thoughtful questions, and fosters an environment that supports learning, innovation, learning from mistakes, and intelligent risk-taking; and exhibits resilience in the face of setbacks.

Drives continuous improvements, supervises the adoption of new technology, and supports digital disruption in line with Walmart’s business model.

jobs.title: Alpha Global Testing - Middle/Front Office - AVP
jobs.description:
State Street is seeking a skilled and proven candidate to lead and work with the team responsible for client conversion and business acceptance testing at the Assistant Vice President level. The role is responsible for providing leadership, project management and oversight of the various Front to Back sub-streams, initiatives and deliverables. This includes planning and overseeing the implementation and project level of sub-streams, execution of project deliverables and producing reporting associated with each to enable the achievement of integration goals and financial synergies.

Major Responsibilities

Provide leadership, management and drive the execution of sub-work stream initiatives within the overall Client Conversion Services workstream
Drive execution through stringent project management and close attention to detail of sub-streams Alpha, Client onboarding and ESP initiatives
Knowledge of Investment Manager Servicing/Transaction Management/Core State Street business offerings
Knowledge of Data Warehousing
Oversee Vendor relationship and Vendor team management
Resolve solution impediments with stakeholders, drive project progress, escalate risks, issues and solutions. Implement project changes and interventions to achieve program goals
Manage preparation for sub-stream governance meetings including project plan consolidation and materials preparations
Provide a complete middle office solution to State Street clients
Prepare and present program/project level executive status reports
Provide asset owners and managers a dynamic, customizable, and scalable self-service platform for all their data needs
Perform financial management oversight of sub-streams to enable achievement of integration financial goals and synergies
Engage effectively with vendor partners for seamless delivery and people management
Mentor team on tools, processes and standards
Perform internal communications using multiple communication channels

Qualifications

Education and Experience

Advanced or Master’s degree preferred
Minimum 10 years financial services experience including project/program management experience
PMP Certification and/or consulting experience required

Skills

Proven leadership and program management skills
Proven strong communication, interpersonal, decision-making and negotiation skills
Ability to work collaboratively across multiple organizations to reach common goals
Organized with the ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment
Competencies required: demonstrated strong project management skills, analytical/problem solving skills, business/industry knowledge, communication versatility, information technology acumen, teamwork and leadership, written and verbal skills
Strong skills in Microsoft Office and able to use advanced features of PowerPoint and Excel

Salary Range

$91,000 - $140,500 Annual

The range quoted above applies to the role in the primary location specified. If the candidate would ultimately work outside of the primary location above, the applicable range could differ.

About State Street

Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success.

We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. As an essential partner in our shared success, you’ll benefit from inclusive development opportunities, flexible work-life support, paid volunteer days, and vibrant employee networks that keep you connected to what matters most. Join us in shaping the future.

Are you looking for a new and rewarding leadership challenge in healthcare? Interior Health has an exciting opportunity for Director, Public Health Operations. The location for the role is flexible with the Interior Health region within regional responsibilities. We are looking for people who want to make a difference in the communities in which they live, work and play. Relocation allowance may be provided, apply today to join our amazing organization who was once again named as BC Top Employer for 2026!

Excellent career prospects

Ensures clear performance objectives and indicators are in place to assess the delivery of services within the designated clinical patient care service areas.
Establishes effective administrative systems for maintaining, evaluating, and reporting on the operations of the portfolio.
Establishes systems and processes to evaluate performance of programs and services aligned with corporate direction.
Ensures compliance with legislation and safety standards to provide a healthy and safe environment for patients and staff.

jobs.title: Director - Compliance Program Governance
jobs.description:
The Director, Compliance Program Governance is responsible for providing strategic leadership, governance, oversight, and continuous improvement for the Enterprise Compliance Program (ECP). The role leads centralized governance activities including program reporting, quality assurance, controls oversight, training, program assessments, and strategy.

The Director ensures the compliance programs continues to operate effectively and remains aligned with regulatory expectations. The role operates at an enterprise-wide level and functions as a senior specialist and thought leader. The role collaborates closely with other risk leaders in enterprise risk. The role is positioned within Legal and Regulatory Compliance (LRC) and reports to the Head, Enterprise Compliance Programs.

Program Governance, Quality Assurance & Controls

Oversees governance and execution of centralized compliance program activities.
Establishes and maintains applicable program standards, procedures, operating models, controls, and methodologies.
Leads independent quality assurance reviews and organizes data for compliance effectiveness assessments
As directed, establishes and reinforces centralized controls supporting compliance programs and governance processes.
Identifies opportunities to strengthen governance, improve data quality, streamline processes, and enhance regulatory compliance capabilities.
Conducts and/or effectively challenges compliance assessments to improve control environments.
May performs and/or oversees monitoring and testing activities to evaluate the effectiveness of compliance controls.
Supports root cause analysis and remediation activities arising from control failures, audit findings, regulatory concerns, and compliance issues.

Enterprise Reporting

Leads development and oversight of compliance metrics included executive, management, committee, and board reporting
Reviews, analyzes, and reports insights on regulatory risk using compliance data, metrics, key risk indicators, and effectiveness assessments.
Establishes governance over compliance reporting processes, methodologies, and data quality controls.
Reports compliance program effectiveness and regulatory risk trends to senior management and governance committees.
Identifies, assesses, escalates, and monitors regulatory risks and compliance issues for timely resolution

Leadership and People Management

Fosters a culture aligned to BMO's purpose, values, strategy, and Winning Culture behaviours by role modeling expected leadership behaviours.
Maintains strong networks internally and externally to identify industry trends, benchmarks, and best practices.
May consult to or serve on enterprise governance committees and leadership forums.
Anticipates future regulatory and industry developments and drives proactive changes to governance frameworks and compliance programs.
Ensures alignment between values and behaviours that foster diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging.
Builds highly collaborative and interdependent teams that partner across functions and operating groups to create value for stakeholders.
Attracts, develops, retains, and enables top talent through coaching, mentorship, succession planning, and career development.
Recognizes and rewards performance, addresses development opportunities, and manages performance improvement where required.
Creates an environment of continuous learning, innovation, engagement, and operational excellence.
Promotes a strong risk and compliance culture across the organization.
Advises and influences senior leaders regarding regulatory risks associated with business decisions, strategic initiatives, transformation activities, and emerging regulatory developments.

Required Qualifications

Typically 10+ years of relevant experience in Compliance, Risk Management, Governance, Audit, Regulatory Affairs, or related disciplines.
Post-secondary degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Extensive knowledge of regulatory compliance frameworks, risk management practices, governance principles, and enterprise compliance programs.
Experience leading enterprise reporting, quality assurance, controls oversight, governance, or compliance program functions.
Exceptional communication, relationship management, critical thinking, and project leadership skills.
Ability to operate effectively in highly regulated and rapidly changing environments.

Preferred Qualifications

CRCM, CAMS, CCEP, CIA, CISA, or equivalent professional certification.
Strong knowledge of regulatory expectations applicable to financial services organizations.
Experience supporting regulatory examinations, audits, and enterprise compliance programs.
Experience with Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) technology platforms and data analytics solutions.

The Director, Compliance Program Governance is responsible for providing strategic leadership, governance, oversight, and continuous improvement for the Enterprise Compliance Program (ECP). The role leads centralized governance activities including program reporting, quality assurance, controls oversight, training, program assessments, and strategy.

Salary:

$120,000.00 - $215,000.00

Pay Type:

Salaried

Salaries will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and qualifications for the role, and may include a commission structure. Salaries for part-time roles will be pro-rated based on number of hours regularly worked. For commission roles, the salary listed above represents BMO Financial Group’s expected target for the first year in this position.

BMO Financial Group’s total compensation package will vary based on the pay type of the position and may include performance-based incentives, discretionary bonuses, as well as other perks and rewards. BMO also offers health insurance, tuition reimbursement, accident and life insurance, and retirement savings plans. As a member of the BMO team you are valued, respected and heard, and you have more ways to grow and make an impact. We strive to help you make an impact from day one – for yourself and our customers. We’ll support you with the tools and resources you need to reach new milestones, as you help our customers reach theirs. jobs.title: Founding Chief Executive Officer (CEO) & Co-Founder | Canada
jobs.description:
Healthy Cosmos

Location:
Toronto or Greater Toronto Area preferred with travel across Canada
Company stage:
Pre-revenue | Live digital healthcare platform – www. BookTeleMed.com

Opportunity:
Founder-level executive leadership with meaningful, performance-aligned equity participation

Millions of Canadians face long waits to access specialist doctors. For people in rural communities, employees working in remote locations, and patients managing complex medical conditions, getting timely specialist guidance can be particularly challenging. We believe there is a meaningful opportunity to help change that.

Healthy Cosmos operates BookTeleMed.com
, a global telehealth platform connecting patients with experienced international specialist doctors across 15+ medical specialties
, providing non-emergency medical consultations and independent second opinions.

We have built the technology platform and established the specialist network.
Now, we're looking for an entrepreneurial CEO & Co-Founder who can build the business.

The Opportunity

This is a pre-revenue healthcare technology venture with an existing foundation and significant commercial ambitions.
We are seeking a hands-on business builder who believes in our mission and can transform BookTeleMed into a scalable, sustainable healthcare business serving Canadians.

What you'll lead:

• Secure our first institutional customers and paying sponsors across employers, insurers, employee benefits providers, healthcare organizations, provincial governments and patient foundations.
• Raise investment capital and develop strategic partnerships.
• Build and execute a commercially viable B2B and B2B2C growth strategy.
• Expand our network of specialist doctors as institutional sponsorship and patient demand grow.
• Build the organization, leadership team, operating model, and financial foundation for sustainable growth.
• Champion patient-centred innovation, clinical trust, and responsible healthcare access.

Who We're Looking For

An entrepreneurial commercial leader with demonstrated experience building businesses, raising investment capital, generating recurring B2B revenue, closing institutional deals, developing strategic relationships, and leading growth with limited resources.
Experience in healthcare technology, insurance, employee benefits, or related industries is highly desirable.
Fundraising experience and established Canadian institutional relationships are strong advantages.

jobs.title: Customer Success Director
jobs.description:
This employer is an HR technology company seeking a Director of Customer Success Managers to own gross retention and net revenue retention across its named and higher-value accounts. Reporting to the VP of Global Customer Success, you will lead a global organisation of managers and customer success managers who protect the customer base, manage renewals and drive expansion.

The Role

• Lead, hire and coach managers of customer success across multiple regions and time zones.
• Set and manage coverage models by account tier, own the annual re-tiering of books and standardise tier-specific playbooks.
• Oversee renewals across the portfolio and move legacy evergreen agreements to standard contractual terms.
• Lead the weekly and monthly risk and churn review with revenue leadership, keeping real-time health signals and remediation plans for at-risk accounts.
• Set rules of engagement with account management, and report retention, net revenue retention and portfolio risk to executive leadership.

What You'll Need

• 10+ years of experience in customer success or account management within B2B SaaS or global services, including 5+ years leading people managers.
• A proven record of protecting and expanding a large customer book with measurable gains in gross and net retention.
• Experience leading distributed teams across regions and designing tiered coverage models, playbooks and scalable operating frameworks.
• Strong executive presence and fluency with Salesforce and customer health data platforms; HR tech, payroll or global expansion experience is preferred.

What's On Offer

• Annual fixed pay of CAD 140,000 – CAD 175,000, plus variable compensation tied to retention.
• Medical, dental and vision insurance, spending accounts, generous paid parental leave and flexible time off.
• A remote-first team, with a sabbatical after five years.

new_jobs.title: Alpha Global Testing - Middle/Front Office - AVP
new_jobs.description:
State Street is seeking a skilled and proven candidate to lead and work with the team responsible for client conversion and business acceptance testing at the Assistant Vice President level. The role is responsible for providing leadership, project management and oversight of the various Front to Back sub-streams, initiatives and deliverables. This includes planning and overseeing the implementation and project level of sub-streams, execution of project deliverables and producing reporting associated with each to enable the achievement of integration goals and financial synergies.

Major Responsibilities

Provide leadership, management and drive the execution of sub-work stream initiatives within the overall Client Conversion Services workstream
Drive execution through stringent project management and close attention to detail of sub-streams Alpha, Client onboarding and ESP initiatives
Knowledge of Investment Manager Servicing/Transaction Management/Core State Street business offerings
Knowledge of Data Warehousing
Oversee Vendor relationship and Vendor team management
Resolve solution impediments with stakeholders, drive project progress, escalate risks, issues and solutions. Implement project changes and interventions to achieve program goals
Manage preparation for sub-stream governance meetings including project plan consolidation and materials preparations
Provide a complete middle office solution to State Street clients
Prepare and present program/project level executive status reports
Provide asset owners and managers a dynamic, customizable, and scalable self-service platform for all their data needs
Perform financial management oversight of sub-streams to enable achievement of integration financial goals and synergies
Engage effectively with vendor partners for seamless delivery and people management
Mentor team on tools, processes and standards
Perform internal communications using multiple communication channels

Qualifications

Education and Experience

Advanced or Master’s degree preferred
Minimum 10 years financial services experience including project/program management experience
PMP Certification and/or consulting experience required

Skills

Proven leadership and program management skills
Proven strong communication, interpersonal, decision-making and negotiation skills
Ability to work collaboratively across multiple organizations to reach common goals
Organized with the ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment
Competencies required: demonstrated strong project management skills, analytical/problem solving skills, business/industry knowledge, communication versatility, information technology acumen, teamwork and leadership, written and verbal skills
Strong skills in Microsoft Office and able to use advanced features of PowerPoint and Excel

Salary Range

$91,000 - $140,500 Annual

The range quoted above applies to the role in the primary location specified. If the candidate would ultimately work outside of the primary location above, the applicable range could differ.

About State Street

Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success.

We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. As an essential partner in our shared success, you’ll benefit from inclusive development opportunities, flexible work-life support, paid volunteer days, and vibrant employee networks that keep you connected to what matters most. Join us in shaping the future.

new_jobs.title: Director | Public Health Operations
new_jobs.description:
Who Are We Looking For

Are you looking for a new and rewarding leadership challenge in healthcare? Interior Health has an exciting opportunity for Director, Public Health Operations. The location for the role is flexible with the Interior Health region within regional responsibilities. We are looking for people who want to make a difference in the communities in which they live, work and play. Relocation allowance may be provided, apply today to join our amazing organization who was once again named as BC Top Employer for 2026!

Some Of The Benefits Of Joining Interior Health

An attractive remuneration package
Excellent career prospects
Employee & Family Assistance Programs
Employer paid training/education opportunities
Employer paid vacation
Employer paid insurance premiums
Extended Health & Dental coverage
Work-life balance
Relocation Allowance may be provided

The salary range for this position is $130,864 (min) to $163,579 (midpoint) to $188,116 (max) per annum, based on 1.0 FTE. Interior Health typically establishes salaries within the minimum and midpoint of the salary range based on qualifications, experience of the applicant, and an internal equity review of the salaries of other employees.

How Will You Create An Impact

Collaborates and negotiates with the MHO and other Medical staff, to develop strategies to ensure quality, evidenced based clinical patient care service delivery to address complex public health issues, improve health outcomes and ensure sustainability of services consistent with the established priorities and the vision, values, and strategic direction of Interior Health.
Fosters strategic relationships and leads negotiations with internal and external partners to establish shared priorities, identify and plan responsive delivery systems and services and to discuss and resolve issues related to same, in support of the effective and efficient integration of healthcare services and resources throughout the organization.
Develops an operational framework for staffing and service delivery through collaborative partnerships that support patient and family centered care, patient safety and quality of care, evidenced based practices, sound risk management, process improvement and optimum utilization management.
Develops and effectively manages capital and operating budgets that complement strategic directions within existing fiscal constraints.
Establishes an effective workforce plan in collaboration with key partners that ensures the ongoing availability of qualified competent staff within the context of operational demands and resource constraints.
Provides overall leadership and direction for operational staff, that supports the achievement of required outcomes, organizational and portfolio priorities, and ensures adherence to accreditation, regulatory, professional and safety standards.
Ensures clear performance objectives and indicators are in place to assess the delivery of services within the designated clinical patient care service areas.
Establishes effective administrative systems for maintaining, evaluating, and reporting on the operations of the portfolio.
Establishes systems and processes to evaluate performance of programs and services aligned with corporate direction.
Ensures compliance with legislation and safety standards to provide a healthy and safe environment for patients and staff.
Responds to patient care issues and public concerns in a supportive and goal-oriented manner, facilitating communication to affect positive outcomes.
Represents assigned operational areas on a variety of internal and external committees as required.
In alignment with IH’s Occupational Health & Safety Program, maintain a healthy and safe work environment through complying with and implementing applicable Occupational Health and Safety Regulation, responding to requests from WSBC, identifying hazards and communicating risks, ensuring compliance with employee training, conducting effective incident investigations, and implementing required corrective actions.
Performs other related duties as assigned.

new_jobs.title: Director - Compliance Program Governance
new_jobs.description:
The Director, Compliance Program Governance is responsible for providing strategic leadership, governance, oversight, and continuous improvement for the Enterprise Compliance Program (ECP). The role leads centralized governance activities including program reporting, quality assurance, controls oversight, training, program assessments, and strategy.

The Director ensures the compliance programs continues to operate effectively and remains aligned with regulatory expectations. The role operates at an enterprise-wide level and functions as a senior specialist and thought leader. The role collaborates closely with other risk leaders in enterprise risk. The role is positioned within Legal and Regulatory Compliance (LRC) and reports to the Head, Enterprise Compliance Programs.

Program Governance, Quality Assurance & Controls

Oversees governance and execution of centralized compliance program activities.
Establishes and maintains applicable program standards, procedures, operating models, controls, and methodologies.
Leads independent quality assurance reviews and organizes data for compliance effectiveness assessments
As directed, establishes and reinforces centralized controls supporting compliance programs and governance processes.
Identifies opportunities to strengthen governance, improve data quality, streamline processes, and enhance regulatory compliance capabilities.
Conducts and/or effectively challenges compliance assessments to improve control environments.
May performs and/or oversees monitoring and testing activities to evaluate the effectiveness of compliance controls.
Supports root cause analysis and remediation activities arising from control failures, audit findings, regulatory concerns, and compliance issues.

Enterprise Reporting

Leads development and oversight of compliance metrics included executive, management, committee, and board reporting
Reviews, analyzes, and reports insights on regulatory risk using compliance data, metrics, key risk indicators, and effectiveness assessments.
Establishes governance over compliance reporting processes, methodologies, and data quality controls.
Reports compliance program effectiveness and regulatory risk trends to senior management and governance committees.
Identifies, assesses, escalates, and monitors regulatory risks and compliance issues for timely resolution

Leadership and People Management

Fosters a culture aligned to BMO's purpose, values, strategy, and Winning Culture behaviours by role modeling expected leadership behaviours.
Maintains strong networks internally and externally to identify industry trends, benchmarks, and best practices.
May consult to or serve on enterprise governance committees and leadership forums.
Anticipates future regulatory and industry developments and drives proactive changes to governance frameworks and compliance programs.
Ensures alignment between values and behaviours that foster diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging.
Builds highly collaborative and interdependent teams that partner across functions and operating groups to create value for stakeholders.
Attracts, develops, retains, and enables top talent through coaching, mentorship, succession planning, and career development.
Recognizes and rewards performance, addresses development opportunities, and manages performance improvement where required.
Creates an environment of continuous learning, innovation, engagement, and operational excellence.
Promotes a strong risk and compliance culture across the organization.
Advises and influences senior leaders regarding regulatory risks associated with business decisions, strategic initiatives, transformation activities, and emerging regulatory developments.

Required Qualifications

Typically 10+ years of relevant experience in Compliance, Risk Management, Governance, Audit, Regulatory Affairs, or related disciplines.
Post-secondary degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Extensive knowledge of regulatory compliance frameworks, risk management practices, governance principles, and enterprise compliance programs.
Experience leading enterprise reporting, quality assurance, controls oversight, governance, or compliance program functions.
Exceptional communication, relationship management, critical thinking, and project leadership skills.
Ability to operate effectively in highly regulated and rapidly changing environments.

Preferred Qualifications

CRCM, CAMS, CCEP, CIA, CISA, or equivalent professional certification.
Strong knowledge of regulatory expectations applicable to financial services organizations.
Experience supporting regulatory examinations, audits, and enterprise compliance programs.
Experience with Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) technology platforms and data analytics solutions.

The Director, Compliance Program Governance is responsible for providing strategic leadership, governance, oversight, and continuous improvement for the Enterprise Compliance Program (ECP). The role leads centralized governance activities including program reporting, quality assurance, controls oversight, training, program assessments, and strategy.

Salary:

$120,000.00 - $215,000.00

Pay Type:

Salaried

The above represents BMO Financial Group’s pay range and type.

Salaries will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and qualifications for the role, and may include a commission structure. Salaries for part-time roles will be pro-rated based on number of hours regularly worked. For commission roles, the salary listed above represents BMO Financial Group’s expected target for the first year in this position.

BMO Financial Group’s total compensation package will vary based on the pay type of the position and may include performance-based incentives, discretionary bonuses, as well as other perks and rewards. BMO also offers health insurance, tuition reimbursement, accident and life insurance, and retirement savings plans. To view more details of our benefits, please visit: https://jobs.bmo.com/global/en/Total-Rewards

About Us

At BMO we are driven by a shared Purpose: Boldly Grow the Good in business and life. It calls on us to create lasting, positive change for our customers, our communities and our people. By working together, innovating and pushing boundaries, we transform lives and businesses, and power economic growth around the world.

As a member of the BMO team you are valued, respected and heard, and you have more ways to grow and make an impact. We strive to help you make an impact from day one – for yourself and our customers. We’ll support you with the tools and resources you need to reach new milestones, as you help our customers reach theirs. From in-depth training and coaching, to manager support and network-building opportunities, we’ll help you gain valuable experience, and broaden your skillset.

To find out more visit us at https://jobs.bmo.com/ca/en

BMO is committed to an inclusive, equitable and accessible workplace. By learning from each other’s differences, we gain strength through our people and our perspectives. Note to Recruiters: BMO does not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than directly from a candidate. Any unsolicited resumes sent to BMO, directly or indirectly, will be considered BMO property. BMO will not pay a fee for any placement resulting from the receipt of an unsolicited resume. new_jobs.title: Founding Chief Executive Officer (CEO) & Co-Founder | Canada
new_jobs.description:
Healthy Cosmos

Location:
Toronto or Greater Toronto Area preferred with travel across Canada
Company stage:
Pre-revenue | Live digital healthcare platform – www. BookTeleMed.com

Opportunity:
Founder-level executive leadership with meaningful, performance-aligned equity participation

Millions of Canadians face long waits to access specialist doctors. For people in rural communities, employees working in remote locations, and patients managing complex medical conditions, getting timely specialist guidance can be particularly challenging. We believe there is a meaningful opportunity to help change that.

Healthy Cosmos operates BookTeleMed.com
, a global telehealth platform connecting patients with experienced international specialist doctors across 15+ medical specialties
, providing non-emergency medical consultations and independent second opinions.

We have built the technology platform and established the specialist network.
Now, we're looking for an entrepreneurial CEO & Co-Founder who can build the business.

The Opportunity

This is a pre-revenue healthcare technology venture with an existing foundation and significant commercial ambitions.
We are seeking a hands-on business builder who believes in our mission and can transform BookTeleMed into a scalable, sustainable healthcare business serving Canadians.

What you'll lead:

• Secure our first institutional customers and paying sponsors across employers, insurers, employee benefits providers, healthcare organizations, provincial governments and patient foundations.
• Raise investment capital and develop strategic partnerships.
• Build and execute a commercially viable B2B and B2B2C growth strategy.
• Expand our network of specialist doctors as institutional sponsorship and patient demand grow.
• Build the organization, leadership team, operating model, and financial foundation for sustainable growth.
• Champion patient-centred innovation, clinical trust, and responsible healthcare access.

Who We're Looking For

An entrepreneurial commercial leader with demonstrated experience building businesses, raising investment capital, generating recurring B2B revenue, closing institutional deals, developing strategic relationships, and leading growth with limited resources.
Experience in healthcare technology, insurance, employee benefits, or related industries is highly desirable.
Fundraising experience and established Canadian institutional relationships are strong advantages.

Apply confidentially:

https://digiaudit.ai/careers/healthy-cosmos

If you've built businesses, believe in improving healthcare access for Canadians, and want to help create something meaningful from the ground up, we'd welcome a conversation.

Build what matters. Lead what comes next.
